strategy_title: Swap 2D Tile Axes to Coalesce Strided Middle-Dim Reduction
strategy_description: When reducing over a middle dimension of a 3D row-major tensor (strides: [D1*D2, D2, 1]), a [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_R] load tile that places the reduction index (stride=D2) on the warp-contiguous axis (axis=1) causes each warp's 32 threads to access memory D2 elements apart, wasting ~87% of L2 sectors (only 4/32 bytes utilized per sector) and saturating L2 throughput above 96%. The fix is to transpose the tile to [BLOCK_R, BLOCK_M] so the output index (stride=1) is the warp-contiguous axis (axis=1), then reduce with tl.sum(vals, axis=0). This collapses L2 throughput from 96% to 51%, raises L1 hit rate from 0.02% to 84.75%, drops warp cycles per instruction from 241 to 9.5, and improves compute throughput from 6.5% to 44.8%.
slow_pseudocode:
# [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_R] tile — r_idx (stride=last_dim) is warp-contiguous (axis=1)
b_idx = batch_idx[:, None]   # [BLOCK_M, 1]
r_idx = r_offsets[None, :]   # [1, BLOCK_R]
c_idx = col_idx[:, None]     # [BLOCK_M, 1]
linear_idx = b_idx*(reduce_dim*last_dim) + r_idx*last_dim + c_idx  # [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_R]
combined_mask = mask_out[:, None] & r_mask[None, :]
vals = tl.load(in_ptr + linear_idx, mask=combined_mask, other=0.0)
acc += tl.sum(vals, axis=1)  # reduce r -> [BLOCK_M]
fast_pseudocode:
# [BLOCK_R, BLOCK_M] tile — col_idx (stride=1) is warp-contiguous (axis=1)
b_idx = batch_idx[None, :]   # [1, BLOCK_M]
r_idx = r_offsets[:, None]   # [BLOCK_R, 1]
c_idx = col_idx[None, :]     # [1, BLOCK_M]
linear_idx = b_idx*(reduce_dim*last_dim) + r_idx*last_dim + c_idx  # [BLOCK_R, BLOCK_M]
combined_mask = mask_out[None, :] & r_mask[:, None]  # [BLOCK_R, BLOCK_M]
vals = tl.load(in_ptr + linear_idx, mask=combined_mask, other=0.0)
acc += tl.sum(vals, axis=0)  # reduce r (axis=0) -> [BLOCK_M]
# Also update autotune: BLOCK_M must be power-of-2 and multiple of 32
applicable_when: Triton kernel reduces over a middle dimension of a 3D row-major tensor (strides [D1*D2, D2, 1]). The load tile is 2D with the reduction index (stride=D2, large) placed on the warp-contiguous axis (axis=1 / last tile dimension). NCU reports UncoalescedGlobalAccess with >80% excessive sectors, MemoryCacheAccessPattern with only 4/32 bytes utilized per sector, L2 throughput >80%, and compute throughput <15%.
do_not_apply_when: The reduction dimension has stride=1 (already coalesced). The tile is already [BLOCK_R, BLOCK_M] with the output index on axis=1. Occupancy is already register-limited and adding BLOCK_M as a large tile dimension would further reduce theoretical occupancy below an acceptable threshold (after the fix, registers per thread rose to 165, limiting theoretical occupancy to 18.75%).
framework_notes: Triton: the warp-contiguous axis is always the last (rightmost) tile dimension (axis=1 for 2D tiles). Broadcasting [:, None] places a vector on axis=0 (slow), [None, :] places it on axis=1 (fast/warp-contiguous). tl.sum(vals, axis=0) reduces the slow axis, leaving the fast axis intact as the output. BLOCK_M must be a power-of-2 and multiple of 32 for full coalescing.

strategy_title: Transpose 2D Load Tile to Coalesce Strided Reduction Axis
strategy_description: When a kernel loads a 2D tile [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_R] where the reduction axis (BLOCK_R) has a large stride in memory (e.g., last_dim elements apart), warp threads access non-contiguous sectors, wasting 87%+ of L2 bandwidth. Transposing the tile to [BLOCK_R, BLOCK_M] so that the contiguous dimension (stride=1) varies along axis=1 (the warp-contiguous axis) eliminates sector waste and reduces warp stall cycles per instruction from ~241 to ~115. This is a minimal 3-line change: flip the broadcast dimensions of the index components and change tl.sum axis from 1 to 0, with no grid or output indexing changes required.
slow_pseudocode:
# [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_R] tile — strided loads
b_idx = batch_idx[:, None]   # [BLOCK_M, 1]
r_idx = r_offsets[None, :]   # [1, BLOCK_R]
c_idx = col_idx[:, None]     # [BLOCK_M, 1]
linear_idx = b_idx*(R*C) + r_idx*C + c_idx  # [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_R]
combined_mask = mask_out[:, None] & r_mask[None, :]
vals = tl.load(ptr + linear_idx, mask=combined_mask)
acc += tl.sum(vals, axis=1)  # reduce over BLOCK_R
fast_pseudocode:
# [BLOCK_R, BLOCK_M] tile — coalesced loads
b_idx = batch_idx[None, :]   # [1, BLOCK_M]
r_idx = r_offsets[:, None]   # [BLOCK_R, 1]
c_idx = col_idx[None, :]     # [1, BLOCK_M]
linear_idx = b_idx*(R*C) + r_idx*C + c_idx  # [BLOCK_R, BLOCK_M]
combined_mask = r_mask[:, None] & mask_out[None, :]
vals = tl.load(ptr + linear_idx, mask=combined_mask)
acc += tl.sum(vals, axis=0)  # reduce over BLOCK_R (axis=0), acc stays [BLOCK_M]
applicable_when: UncoalescedGlobalAccess rule fires with 80%+ excessive sectors; MemoryCacheAccessPattern shows only 4/32 bytes utilized per sector; L2 throughput >90% saturated while compute <15%; the strided dimension is the reduction axis (not the output axis); a single CTA owns all reduction iterations for its output elements (no atomics needed).
do_not_apply_when: The reduction axis is already the contiguous (stride=1) dimension in memory; when BLOCK_M=1 (no 2D tile to transpose); when the kernel uses atomics for partial reductions across CTAs (transposing alone won't fix correctness); when the output axis has a large stride instead of the reduction axis.
framework_notes: Triton-specific: tl.sum(vals, axis=0) reduces over the first dimension of the 2D tile. The broadcast notation [:, None] vs [None, :] controls which axis is contiguous for warp threads. Registers per thread dropped from 32 to 23 as a side effect of the simpler index expression, improving block limit from 16 to 21 blocks/SM.

strategy_title: evict_first Cache Hint for Streaming Reduction Loads
strategy_description: Adding eviction_policy='evict_first' to streaming reduction loads is expected to reduce L1/L2 cache pollution from non-reused data, but in this case the profiling data shows the kernel actually became ~4% slower (6.15ms → 6.42ms) despite the reported 2.38x speedup label. The L1 hit rate dropped from 84.75% to 73.07% and L2 hit rate increased from 42.27% to 55.12%, suggesting evict_first caused more L2 pressure rather than relieving it. The kernel remained bottlenecked on L1/TEX throughput (~91-93%) with no meaningful improvement in scheduler eligibility or compute throughput, indicating that evict_first alone cannot overcome the fundamental register-pressure-limited occupancy (18.75%) and residual uncoalesced access patterns.
slow_pseudocode:
# Without eviction hint
for r_start in range(0, reduce_dim, BLOCK_R):
    vals = tl.load(in_ptr + linear_idx, mask=combined_mask, other=0.0)
    acc += tl.sum(vals, axis=0)
fast_pseudocode:
# With evict_first hint on streaming loads
for r_start in range(0, reduce_dim, BLOCK_R):
    vals = tl.load(in_ptr + linear_idx, mask=combined_mask, other=0.0,
                   eviction_policy='evict_first')
    acc += tl.sum(vals, axis=0)
applicable_when: Streaming reduction where input data far exceeds L2 capacity, L1/TEX throughput is saturated >90%, L2 hit rate is low (<50%), and the kernel is memory-bandwidth bound with high reuse of accumulator data. Most effective when occupancy is not register-limited and there is genuine cache pollution from non-reused streaming data.
do_not_apply_when: The kernel is already register-limited (e.g., 165 registers/thread, 18.75% theoretical occupancy) and L1 hit rate is already high (>80%) due to prior coalescing fixes. In this regime, evict_first drops L1 hit rate (84.75% → 73.07%) and increases L2 pressure, causing a net regression. Also avoid when uncoalesced access patterns remain the dominant bottleneck — fix coalescing first.
framework_notes: Triton: eviction_policy='evict_first' is a PTX-level cache hint that marks loaded cache lines for immediate eviction after use. It is a pure semantic hint with no correctness impact. Do NOT apply to tl.store for outputs that downstream kernels may reuse. On H200/Hopper, this maps to the NVIDIA evict-first sector eviction policy in L1/L2.
